correctness.rationale: The proof begins with the classical symmetric determinantal degree product and rewrites it factorially. For each prime p dividing n, a direct Legendre-floor calculation proves that the corank p^{nu_p(n)} degree is a p-unit whenever that corank is proper. This excludes every possible common prime unless n is a prime power, and the rank-one quadratic Veronese degree excludes odd prime powers. For n=2^e, an exact adjacent-corank ratio gives a closed two-adic formula for every even corank; a proved binary digit-sum inequality yields the lower bound e-1, odd coranks are strictly more divisible, and corank two has valuation exactly e-1. The bundled exact checker independently verifies all full tower gcds through n=120 and the valuation identities for powers of two through n=256.

value.rationale: The symmetric determinantal loci form the full secant/rank stratification of the quadratic Veronese family, and each projective degree is the generic complementary linear-section count of one rank stratum. Their gcd is therefore the exact universal divisibility shared by all proper symmetric-rank enumerative counts at fixed matrix size. The theorem gives a sharp global phase transition: nontrivial universal divisibility occurs only at power-of-two sizes, and the exact common divisor is n/2 for every power of two beyond n=2. This is a natural whole-tower invariant and is not a routine restatement of a single-degree formula.
